items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: We were playing for the Spike Brothers... Reb Spikes was the tenor player... Ori and I at 4th and Stanford in Los Angeles.

ctx.x: Mm-hmm. Um, what about, uh, the raids out in California that you told me about? Thanks. Mm-hmm.

We were playing at, uh, at the Dreamland Cafe, nightclub, you know. Mm-hmm. We were playing for the Spike Brothers. You heard of them. Mm-hmm. We were playing for the Spike Brothers. Ori and I at 4th and Stanford in Los Angeles. I'll never forget that. And, uh, we were playing there one night, one Sunday night, I'll never forget it. And the police had told, Reb Spikes was the tenor player, you see. Yeah, Reb Spikes, Reb and Johnny. Johnny was the oldest brother. Reb was a tall, nice-looking boy. And he had told…

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: Well, we played at the Dreamland for them. You see, after we left the Cadillac, we went down and played for Spikes. Spike Brothers.

ctx.x: He was in Los Angeles at that time.
At that very time. What do you know about that? The Spikes Brothers, did you meet them? Spike Brothers, yeah.

Red Spikes, yeah. Johnny Spikes, yeah. Well, we played at the Dreamland for them. You see, after we left the Cadillac, we went down and played for Spikes. Spike Brothers. And they raided that John and police beat Johnny Spikes, so it was terrible. He was a tenor man. Beat himself in terrible. I never forget that. Yeah? Yes, indeed. What were they raided for?
